voiceover:
[curious] An open-source Google Analytics replacement now makes about $10K a month.

And the move behind it sounds like it should lose money. Stay for it.

It's called Rybbit. Cookieless analytics, so no cookie banner, with session replay and funnels. Self-hosting is free, and teams pay for the hosted cloud.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR: about $10K in MRR, $9K in the last 30 days, 342 subscriptions, and 25% growth.

It's built by indie developer Bill Yang.

How'd it grow? The code is public on GitHub, and one review says it hit 5,000 stars in nine days. The homepage also has a live demo, so you can try it without signing up.

Steal two things. Put a live demo on your landing page. And name who you're replacing, right in your tagline.

[serious] Honest catch: revenue isn't profit, and Google Analytics is free. Cloud starts at $13 a month billed annually, after a 7-day trial.

[whispers] So the move? He gave the product away. The free, open code earned trust, and that trust turned into paying cloud customers.

Would you build this, or just self-host it? Send this to the friend who keeps saying they'll start a SaaS.

Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Rybbit — Open source Google Analytics replacement

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Rybbit — Open source Google Analytics replacement
pick.angle: An open-source Google Analytics replacement went from zero to about $10K/month, and anyone can read the code

research.what_it_does: Open-source, cookieless web and product analytics that replaces Google Analytics. It includes session replay, funnels, web vitals and error tracking, and you can self-host it.
research.who_pays: Small teams, professional teams and enterprises that want privacy-friendly analytics with no cookie banner. They pay for the hosted cloud version, which is paid-only after a 7-day trial. Self-hosting is free.
research.pricing: Per rybbit.com/pricing, with a pageview slider starting at 100,000 monthly pageviews. Standard is $13/month billed annually, with up to 5 websites and 3 team members. Pro is $26/month billed annually, with unlimited websites and team members, session replays, 5 year data retention, 5x higher API rate limit and priority support. Enterprise is custom. There is a 7-day free trial, and no credit card is charged until the trial ends. Third-party reviews put month-to-month pricing at $19 for Standard and $39 for Pro, and the pricing page says annual billing gets 4 months free.
growth: The founder posted on X (@yang_frog) on Jul 1, 2025 that he launched Rybbit on Product Hunt that day. He cited 7k GitHub stars in under 2 months.

Product Hunt tracker hunted.space lists a launch on October 19th, 2025 with 586 upvotes and #1 Product of the Day. The tagline then read '9k Github Stars'. A third-party review (doolpa.com) says an earlier Product Hunt launch took #2 of the day. The sources conflict, and the Jul 1, 2025 launch rank is unverified.

Hacker News: a Show HN-style post (item 43918620) where Bill Yang says he worked on it for 4 months and only publicly launched a few days earlier. He says he is 'happy to collect stars for the time being'. A commenter there accuses Rybbit of fingerprinting users.

The open-source repo drove distribution. A third-party review says it hit 5,000 GitHub stars within nine days of launch, per doolpa.com, and a second review says it crossed 10,000 stars in under a year. GitHub now shows about 13.3k stars, and Trendshift shows 13.2k with 53 contributors.

Podcast Trial to Paid (episode 1) says Bill 'engineered a viral launch with zero ad spend'. It says he hit $1.6K in revenue 35 days after launch, and credits smart moves like embedding a live demo directly in the landing page. The homepage still has a 'Live demo' linking to demo.rybbit.com.
Bill's own X metrics on Jul 4, 2025, two months after public launch: $638 MRR, $2,360 revenue (higher because of annual plans), 34 paying customers, 1,481 sites added, 7,262 GitHub stars.
He also listed the product on AppSumo, where his message says it started as an open-source project and grew faster than expected.

Feature-led content and SEO: many third-party comparison and review sites (travis.media, analytics-alternatives.com, doolpa) compare Rybbit with Plausible and GA4. Each feature has its own page, such as session replay and error tracking. These pages are on the site, and no source says SEO was a deliberate strategy.
founder_story: Bill Yang is a solo indie developer based in California. His own site says he has a computer science degree and 4 years of experience in software engineering. It says he is an 'independent builder at its core'.
His site says he was unhappy with Google Analytics and other analytics tools, so he built his own and open sourced it.

Before Rybbit he built the gaming stats site Tomato.gg, which he describes as 1.5M sessions/month (Trial to Paid podcast summary). The same summary says he once thought he was 'too dumb to code' in high school.
He worked on Rybbit for about 4 months before the public launch (his own Hacker News comment). A third-party review says it went public on April 15, 2025 after roughly 110 days of development.

His LinkedIn work history and the AppSumo profile say Rybbit started in January 2025, and the AppSumo profile says 'Bootstrapped'. The AppSumo page also signs off 'Bill & the Rybbit team', so team size is unclear.
lessons: Open source works as a distribution channel. A free self-hostable repo built GitHub stars (5k in nine days, 13k+ now), and those stars turned into trust and paying cloud customers.
Put a live demo on the landing page. Rybbit's homepage and feature pages link to demo.rybbit.com so visitors can try it without signing up.

Position against a known incumbent in the product tagline ('Open source Google Analytics replacement'). Add the feature that rivals like Plausible lack, which is session replay on Pro, and be transparent about your price.
Build in public with real numbers. Bill posted MRR, customers and star counts on X, even with a small following (765 followers), which gave the project credibility and press.
Relaunch on Product Hunt when you have major updates. Bill used a repeat launch and the star count, such as '9k Github Stars' and 'Help us get to 10k stars', as a call to action.
criticism: Competition is heavy: Plausible, Fathom, Umami, Matomo, PostHog, Mixpanel and Google Analytics itself, which is free. GA4 shows 'Free*' at 100K pageviews in one review's comparison table.

Because the code is open under AGPL-3.0, anyone can self-host it for free. Bill himself flagged AGPL as less permissive than MIT in a Hacker News post. He also reported a copycat on X on Jul 24, 2025 that copied the landing page feature cards.

Critics on Hacker News raised a claim that it fingerprints users, and others complained about AGPL licensing and event-based cloud billing (doolpa.com summary). One G2 reviewer says event-based tracking can feel constraining because pageviews pile up. These are user opinions, not verified findings.
Revenue is not profit. The $9,014 in 30-day revenue says nothing about profit, hosting costs (Hetzner, ClickHouse) or the cost of Bill's time.

Revenue ≠ product-market fit forever: star growth appears to be slowing, with Trendshift showing about +290 stars in 61 days (Aug 29 – Oct 28, 2026), compared with 5,000 in the first nine days. That is the writer's inference from the figures.
facts: GitHub repo rybbit-io/rybbit is TypeScript and licensed AGPL-3.0, with about 13.3k stars and 783 forks (the page snapshot may be dated).

Third-party review claims: over 10,000 organizations use it and over 12,000 GitHub stars (travis.media). Another review (doolpa) cites more than 4,000 organisations according to the company. These counts conflict and are not verified.
Cloud hosting is EU-hosted (Germany). It uses a ~6KB tracker (analytics-alternatives.com).
The product has added features since launch, including error tracking, an MCP server for AI agents, and uptime monitoring, which Bill teased on X on Jul 25, 2025.
Rybbit's Pro tier includes session replay, and Plausible, Fathom and Umami don't offer replay at any price (analytics-alternatives.com, May 2026).
do_not_claim: Team size (Bill calls himself the creator, but signs 'Bill & the Rybbit team' on AppSumo)
Exact number of customers or organizations using it (sources conflict: 4,000 vs 10,000+)
That it took #1 or #2 on Product Hunt on the July 2025 launch (sources conflict; only the Oct 19, 2025 #1 is documented by hunted.space)
That SEO or Reddit drove growth (no founder source)
The founding date: TrustMRR says January 2024, but Bill's own site and AppSumo say January 2025, so say 2025 or avoid the year
That the cloud has a free tier (some third-party sites claim one, but the official pricing page shows only a 7-day trial)
Exact current GitHub star count; it moves, so say 'over 13k' only if rechecked
research.notes: Hook idea: a solo dev built an open-source Google Analytics replacement, and it now does about $9.6K MRR with 342 subscriptions (TrustMRR data). Most growth details come from the founder's own X posts and a podcast summary, not independent press. TrustMRR says founded January 2024, but the founder's site and AppSumo say January 2025, so avoid stating the year or say 'launched publicly in 2025'. The founder's X handle is @yang_frog (TrustMRR left it blank), and his X profile snippet was cached, so the follower count comes from TrustMRR. Pricing pages show annual-billed prices ($13 and $26) as the headline, and monthly billing is $19 and $39 per third-party sites, so say 'from $13/mo billed annually'. The homepage also lists 'Start for $0', which is the free trial, not a free plan. Some third-party sites show a different free tier, which is outdated or wrong. The rybbit.io domain still appears in the app's API host and in older podcast notes.
